conclusions: A current-source committed virtual-range gap is observed in ALL THREE densities for this buffer-local prepend, including Table's stable image-ID row-key path. It is not only a Justified key-label phenomenon.

In each first publication commit the photographs' new rows are outside the chosen rows and none of the shared photographs is in the region DOM. After compensation all return, but with new image elements. Stable labels alone cannot retain elements omitted from rendering in this path.

Grid/Justified also have an intermediate committed snapshot with corrected DOM scrollTop but the old chosen row set. This witnesses the DOM/virtual-range coordination gap; it does not establish when either snapshot was painted.

No src mutation of the original img nodes is observed here. Do not describe this result as demonstrated in-place source swapping. Detached card ancestry can change independently from the old img's src/lifetime.

Key/parent identity breaks can coexist or matter where row sets overlap. The test does not establish that every suggested stable-key change is useless, that A0+K is the only repair, or that direct render-time mutation of virtualizer.scrollOffset is safe.

Spatial correctness and image-element lifetime are distinct. Fixed Grid slot handling is not proof of retained img identity. Prior per-layout B2 benefit/cost results remain valid, but scope recommendations cannot be justified by claiming only Justified has this lifetime interruption.

b2GeometryLifetime20261021.question: Can a visibility-scoped block hold keep truthful dimensions, release without moving other visible blocks, and avoid surviving incompatible navigation?

conditions.data: Existing seamCorpus, mixed ratios including 10:1 and 0.67:1; synthetic IDs only. No live reads or browser use.
conditions.backward: Four cases: 390/1120px, indexed/seek. Seed global48..191, partial44..191, completed0..191. Exactly4 of48 boundary dimensions initially known. Test-only spy holds original packing inputs for one build; actual dimensions remain authoritative.
conditions.forward: Two cases at390/1120px: partial0..51 then completed0..143; test-only hold of the second block. First known row is a negative control, not presumed unstable.
conditions.lifecycle: One case characterizes existing factual dimension snapshot through resize, re-entry, full-block eviction, return with missing boundary dimensions, different query, disjoint seek, regime change and reorder.
conditions.scope: Only the existing unit test file changed under src. No runtime hold state, product policy, metadata-fetch change, browser fixture or campaign-history change. Mocked packing is always restored.

findings: Holding the original block inputs retains the four original known-image box shapes while real new dimensions publish separately. Newly known images can occupy square provisional boxes despite nonsquare authoritative ratios.
Original-cohort departure is insufficient: a row of newly known images in the same held block can be visible after all four original images leave; release changes those new boxes.

After releasing the prefix block, all items48..191 retain left/width/height and receive one identical vertical translation in all four mixed-ratio controls. This is geometry evidence for existing compensation, not DOM timing or unclamped-scroll certification.
The first known forward row remains identical after real dimensions replace estimates at both widths. Partial-block status alone is not evidence that a visible row needs a hold.

Existing factual snapshots preserve real ratios through width changes and compatible re-entry, drop fully evicted blocks, and discard incompatible query/overlap/regime/reorder context. They contain no presentation lifetime or navigation generations.

b2StabilityFilmstrip20261021.question: Do already-visible thumbnails show intermediate content or move when a backward page publishes, and which mechanism explains a positive finding?

conditions.application: Current product policy and source files unchanged; local app on3041,70000 synthetic records,1000-image retention. No live-service reads. B1/F1, two lower eager rows, five-row overscan and upper/rest lazy behavior fixed.

Each app capture separately injects a wrong image and8px displacement for150ms, restores both, and requires their detection. Important CSS priority makes the displacement effective; original value/priority restored. Deliberate errors excluded from normal cohort observations.
conditions.positions: Edge controls stop at the temporary loaded-data wall; interior controls place the viewport around buffer-local index96 and admit a legitimate programmatic backward read. No blanket unmarked-demand veto. Both layouts retain their normal compensation.
conditions.transport: Normal routes use local generated images. Inline uses data URLs to remove image HTTP transport, not to emulate production cache policy. Held-repeat arms would delay repeat requests for target images by200ms, but no such requests occurred: treatment unsupported, not proof of delay tolerance.
conditions.counterfactual: Justified-only frozen-boundary arm substitutes the48 original ratios in one affected block in the intercepted fixture module response. It holds estimates during this observation only; no product toggle, key change, permanent freeze or geometry-lifetime design selected.
conditions.limits: Compositor delivery is sparse, not every physical display frame. Calibration demonstrates150ms wrong-image/shift detection, not guaranteed single-frame detection. Large capture gaps include unchanged-screen intervals and cannot certify absence of shorter glitches. Unknown pixels mean an unclassifiable complementary pair, not necessarily blank imagery. Headless/local data and marked PNGs do not certify live photo performance or native trackpad behavior.
conditions.rounding: All saved numeric fields rounded to three decimals. Frame times are action-relative, not epoch timestamps. Cases are individual controls, not population-tail estimates.

findings: Both layouts' fully known interior controls retained the sampled image colors and anchor marker through publication, despite DOM image replacement. This is bounded evidence, not a universal no-flash guarantee.

Justified's visible boundary image changed box geometry while the central anchor remained stable. Same ordinal-100/block-144:4 known dimensions became48, and44 default square ratios became4:3. Its box moved horizontally and shrank; a sampled point moved95.805px horizontally/14.38px vertically. Its own source stayed correct; another image occupied the old screen point. This is an observed boundary-layout change, not a proven wrong-source flash.

Holding only that block's original ratios removed the sampled movement and changed/unknown identity pairs while DOM replacement still occurred. That isolates a specific geometry cause, not a reason for a global key rewrite or generic packing diagnosis. The control deliberately retains provisional shapes for new neighbors and is not shippable as-is.

No already-visible target image was re-requested. In ordinary interior controls,30 Grid/55 Justified image requests were all for new-page records outside both the original buffer and final mounted rows. Intermediate render-state admission is a lead; extra speculative image work is not automatically harmful or wasted and is not a production byte estimate.

The repeat-request delay arms did not exercise their delay. Their stable pictures cannot establish tolerance of slow repeated image fetches. Inline transport-free controls are separately labelled, not presented as a verified production warm-cache model.

Centre-anchor correctness alone is insufficient for the operator's broader no-swimming goal. The boundary image can move and resize even with a stable anchor. Before product selection, define how visible provisional geometry survives new dimensions and when it may be recomputed.

b2Publication20261021.question: Does backward publication disturb images that were already visible, including at capacity during movement and reversal?

conditions.policy: Current backward admission only; one held backward page. B1/F1, two lower eager rows, upper/rest lazy, five-row overscan and retention limits unchanged. No product edits or packing changes.
conditions.data: 70000 synthetic records, uniform4:3 metadata; ordinary initial buffer300, capacity1000. Local app on3041; all service traffic blocked.
conditions.media: Existing synthetic400x300 SVG and existing image-loader/test/resources/guardian-turner.jpg, intercepted locally at unique per-image fixture URLs. Original visible cohort explicitly loaded/decoded before capture. Routing disables ordinary HTTP caching; this is not a production warm-cache or CDN cost model.
conditions.observation: Browser-local identity cohort, at most128 images and512 frame samples; URLs/identities never serialized.300ms no-publication baseline, then at least500ms after publication. Existing thumbnail and bounded CDP request probes; aggregate requests cover the whole window, not only retained cohort images.
conditions.moving: 400ms at-1000px/s with held page released after80ms, then400ms at+1000px/s. Publication must occur inside first driver interval. Optional applied-step trace capped at2048 excludes compensation; positions are adjusted for applied input and CSS translate.
conditions.pixels: Separate stopped JPEG controls capture a crop before publication, a hidden-image calibration and a post-publication crop. PNGs retained only in memory and compared using browser-native canvas decoding. Original native decode promise is returned unchanged; lifetime timing only. Screenshot intervention changes timing/traffic, so never pool with ordinary controls.
conditions.scope: Headless local Playwright,1720x960. No native-trackpad, real-photo population, compositor-gap duration or live performance certification. Numeric fields rounded to three decimals; exposure is a ratio. Individual runs, not population tails.

findings: Every retained cohort image acquired a replacement DOM image in both layouts, below capacity as well as at capacity. Stored URLs stayed unchanged; stationary baselines had zero readiness waits. This shared effect cannot require Justified packing and cannot be attributed solely to eviction.

Existing image/source/element-generation counters were zero in stopped runs despite wholesale replacement: they compare prior generations on the same DOM element, not identity continuity across new elements. Zero is not proof of retained nodes.

At aligned capacity, sampled anchor displacement after subtracting driven input was below1px in both layouts during continued motion/reversal; one read, bounded retention, far-end eviction and endpoint placement assertions passed. This is bounded current-policy ownership evidence, not arbitrary-speed or candidate certification.

The below-capacity Grid fixture started at column remainder1 and prepended199 images into six columns. Its303px non-anchor row change is an alignment transition, not Justified packing. Justified's19.094px non-anchor shift is retained separately; no packing diagnosis or packing change selected.

Non-pixel controls recorded zero missing/unloaded retained images at sampled frames, but gaps between samples do not prove continuous paint readiness. Publication observations reported117-150ms waits and30-70 whole-window media starts, with zero baseline starts and zero pending at end. Routed local-cache conditions prevent production refetch/byte conclusions or attribution of every request to retained images.

Pixel controls were late for the native-decode interval: both pending flags were false before capture. Hidden-image calibration was sensitive, but nearly identical post-publication pixels do not disprove an earlier blank frame. Native decode itself took1.9/2.4ms and was initiated167/147ms after publication in these instrumented controls; do not label the longer observation as native decode duration.

Screenshot/calibration controls changed request counts and sampled loading compared with ordinary controls; their exposure/frame values are not pooled. No source-key, packing, eager-band, buffer-size, prediction-budget or measurement-definition change is selected.
b2Publication20261021.nextQuestion: Is the shared publication-to-current-image-request interval a real visible disruption under validated cache conditions, and which renderer/browser step owns it? Use a bounded action-owned trace/cohort association, not a packing rewrite or a global content-key substitution. Preserve the existing seek/history protections around positional keys.

interpretationNotes: pendingAtEntry means not loaded (complete/naturalWidth), not explicit decode or exact paint; blank exposure and decodeLead use the existing decoded-thumbnail observer.
blankPct is viewport slot area; very small treatment values can be dominated by the initial observer/decode settling frame. Do not rank tiny differences as reliable policy improvements.
Request lead is milliseconds from CDP request start to first observed slot entry; positive means the request started before entry. decodeLeadPx is measured at decode readiness, not at entry.

Requests and CDP encodedDataLength bytes include setup and recovery. kB means decimal kilobytes at the browser boundary, not backend work. Unexposed means not exposed during measured motion, not never viewed or permanently wasted.
Policy order is balanced, but upstream caches and live delivery are not frozen. Four windows are not a population tail estimate or an exhaustive aspect-ratio corpus.
Resident replay isolates image readiness and excludes real refill/eviction costs. Programmatic smooth scrolling is not native trackpad, reversal, mobile or hosted-CDN certification.

Two extra rows removed pending-at-entry images in this matrix, but faster Justified frame costs persisted without heavy observers. The additional warm controls narrow that cost to runtime media arrival; they do not certify a production loading policy.
